newsitem.title: GREECE: Sarandopoulos says orderbook at 50 bln drs.
newsitem.headline: Sarandopoulos says orderbook at 50 bln drs.

text.p: Construction firm K.I.Sarandopoulos said its first half profit rose 8.2 percent to 841 million drachmas on stronger turnover growth of 30 percent at 4.2 billion.

The company saw equity capital rise to 10.1 billion drachmas from 9.53 billion in the first half a year earlier and its fixed assets increase to 3.95 billion from 2.9 billion drachmas, reflecting investments of one billion, it said.

"The company's financial ratios show significant improvement especially during unfavourable market conditions for the construction sector. It should be noted that it has marginal debt liabilities," it said.
Sarandopoulos plans a 3.0 billion drachma, five-year convertible bond issue by year-end. It said prospects were healthy and its project order book stood at 50.1 billion drachmas.
Among the most important projects it was awarded during the first half it included the following:
The Rio-Antirio bridge where it has a 5.0 percent participation in the Gefyra consortium.
The new Athens international airport at Spata where it is presently carrying out earthmoving works on behalf of Hochtief.

Its involvement in the study and construction of the Elefsis-Stavros-Spata highway, linking Athens with its new airport and budgeted at 397 billion drachmas. Sarandopoulos has a 6.2 percent stake in the Attiki Odos consortium.
Tunnel construction for Greek state railways (OSE) at Platamonas-Leptokaria budgeted at 26.6 billion drachmas. It has an 11.6 percent stake in the consortium, it said.

Other projects include a section of the Patras-Athens-Thessaloniki highway at Aerino budgeted at 18.4 billion drachmas -- participation 8.75 percent -- and renovation work of Rina airport at Tirana, Albania, budgeted at 2.5 billion drachmas.
Shares of Sarandopoulos closed at 1,930 drachmas on Thursday, down 20.
